items.title: 56711_Buster Smith oral history interview
items.q: you were mainly using your brother Boston(?) on piano, weren't you? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah.

ctx.x: So I wrote it out, and had the chords there. I said, 'Boston, listen. We got to play this. The man told us don't come back up here unless we have that 'Rainy Night In Georgia.' And both bosses, a colored boy and the White man too. And I said, 'We got to have it.' And I said, 'Now, look here. I'm going to write them chords out simple.' And I just put them down there, and I didn't put no accidental or nothin' like that. I just put it down there, if it says A, if there's a B-flat and all that, and an A-flat and…

But some of them girls came in there and brought some piano music that we was playing a party downtown there, not too long ago. And they brought one of them numbers that they hear ....(?).... all the time. The man's son got married that night, had a big wedding there, and they had this White girl who wanted to sing this number for this couple. And they was going to catch
